title: Telemetry: ingest + validate A/B experiment exposure events (schema v1)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: This PR adds first-class ingestion support for experiment exposure events emitted from the gateway for route-level A/B testing. It introduces schema v1 validation, PII/safety enforcement, and storage/aggregation-ready tables while keeping overhead low and avoiding cardinality blowups. Context: gateway emission is landing separately (PR #18371). This change is the backend half needed for Console reporting + guardrails. Implementation notes: (1) Adds `ab_exposure_event.v1` to the unified event registry with explicit required fields and an allowlist of dimensions permitted to land in metrics/warehouse. (2) Validates event payloads at ingest (type checking + bounds) and drops/soft-fails invalid events with counters rather than poisoning the pipeline. (3) Enforces privacy constraints from ADR-0188: rejects raw user identifiers, strips unexpected headers, and only allows hashed/stable assignment keys; records `assignment_key_present` as a boolean for debugging docs rather than storing the key. (4) Adds schema versioning + forward-compat behavior: unknown `schema_version` is routed to a quarantine topic with sampling; v1 is accepted; v0 is rejected with a clear error code to speed rollout debugging. (5) Writes to `telemetry.ab_exposure_events` (hot path) and `warehouse.ab_exposure_events_v1` (batch) with partitioning on `event_date` and clustering on `experiment_id` for query patterns used by Console results API. (6) Adds metrics for ingest health: accepted/dropped/quarantined counts by reason, plus lag and size distributions. Rollout plan: deploy pipeline first (this PR), then enable gateway emission behind `ab_exposure_emit_v1` (10% sampling) in staging, then production with default sampling 1% for Hosted and 5% for Dedicated dogfood projects; sampling and allowlist are config-driven. Backfill: none (events are new); results UI should tolerate missing historical data. Testing: unit tests for validation + privacy rules, integration tests covering end-to-end decode -> validate -> write, and a replay test using captured staging payloads. Checklist: [x] Schema reviewed with Telemetry/Analytics (Logan/Mei) [x] Privacy review with Security (Marcus) [x] Cardinality review alignment with Observability (Allison) [x] Runbook note: see `docs/internal/telemetry/ab_exposure_ingest.md` for troubleshooting dropped/quarantined events.
commits: ingest/validator: enforce required fields, bounds, allowlisted dimensions
ingest/privacy: reject PII-like fields + unexpected headers; add drop reasons
warehouse: add ab_exposure_events_v1 table + partitions/clustering + writer
metrics: ingest health counters + quarantine routing + dashboards hooks
tests: validation fixtures + replay tests from staging captures
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we make the drop/quarantine reasons stable strings? Console/reporting and alerting will depend on them; avoid free-form errors. Also please confirm we are not persisting any assignment key material beyond a boolean. Caleb Johnson (author): Yep. Updated to use a typed enum for `drop_reason` with a strict mapping; removed any propagation of raw validation errors. For assignment key: we only store `assignment_key_present` and `assignment_key_source` (enum: api_key_id, project_id, request_id) for debugging docs; no hashes stored. Allison Grant (review): Concerned about dimension allowlist: `route` can explode cardinality if it’s the full path with tenant prefixes. We should store a normalized route key (route_id) not the raw path, and enforce max length. Caleb Johnson (author): Good catch. Updated validator to reject `route_path` entirely; only accepts `route_id` (server-assigned), plus `api_route` enum for legacy endpoints. Added max length checks and a counter for attempted `route_path` usage so we can catch older gateway builds. Nadia Rahman (review): For cost attribution we’ll join on request_id. Do we store request_id here? If yes, what are retention implications? If no, how will we correlate exposures to per-request cost? Caleb Johnson (author): We do NOT store raw request_id in the warehouse table. Hot path can optionally include a short-lived correlation id (rotating) but it’s disabled by default. For cost attribution comparisons, we aggregate independently by experiment/variant at the metrics layer (see follow-up PR #18403). This ingestion PR keeps exposure events as exposures + basic request timing fields only (no per-request cost join). Marcus Lin (review): Please document the privacy posture explicitly (PII constraints, rejection behavior) and add a unit test that ensures unknown fields are dropped not stored. Caleb Johnson (author): Added a dedicated section to `docs/internal/telemetry/ab_exposure_ingest.md` and added a test asserting unknown fields cause quarantine (not partial acceptance) unless they’re in the explicitly ignored list. Mei Lin (review): Warehouse table clustering on experiment_id is good. Can we also cluster on `variant_id` to speed comparisons? Caleb Johnson (author): Added `variant_id` to clustering keys; confirmed migration dry run is fine. Final review from Logan: LGTM once CI green. CI note: integration-tests initially failed due to migration ordering; fixed by moving the migration into the telemetry migration bundle and reran. Approvals: Logan Wright approved; Allison Grant approved; Marcus Lin approved; Mei Lin approved; Nadia Rahman approved. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal-only: Telemetry pipeline can now ingest and store `ab_exposure_event.v1` with validation/quarantine, enabling upcoming Console A/B experiment reporting. No customer-facing change until gateway emission flag is enabled.
